items.title: Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1959-01-02
items.q: Myself, my brother, Eddie, and my cousin, Emil Bones. We was a member of the Chris Kelly band.

ctx.x: We'll talk about that in a minute there.

Yeah, I was off with him in Pensacola, Florida for quite a while. Then I also, I wasn't a member with the Sam Morgan Band, but I did go on a trip with him because his bandit player was Waken and couldn't get off. Was that Davis? That Johnny Dave. Dave. Johnny Dave, yeah. And I made a lot of trouble with the Sam Morgan Band, and I was a regular member of the Chris Kelly jazz band. Myself, my brother, Eddie, and my cousin, Emil Bones. We was a member of the Chris Kelly band. We had a wonderful jazz band.
Was Kid Howard in it at that time? No, Kid Howard, no. He meant later when he was a drummer.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: That was that boy? Lawrence. Lawrence Marrero.

ctx.x: Was he good blues man? I don't know, there was no time on track. The moment was just enough. He may say when someone comes back.

Yes. Didn't want to be very tall. And he had a banjo? That was that boy? Lawrence. Lawrence Marrero. Lawrence Marrero. With Kelly. Anybody else? He's bass playing with Adam Marrero. So you had two Marrero's in the band. Yeah. One time I had two. Marrero in the fridge.
Sorry he was playing with. Sorry he played with Kelly too? Yeah. Well who usually played drums? I played drums with Kelly.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: Which cousin? Lawrence. Wake with Lawrence and wake with John too.

ctx.x: He was lively and still, you know.

Well on the stand, on the music stand, he stood lively. He stayed there and he danced on them drums and he had everything going and his temper was there and he never nausea out. Never get up on that cymbal and swing your eye on him, man. He worked that cymbal in there, he stood there dancing on him, he exploded like a fool and bust out and laughed. He said, he said, how about you, brother-in-law, let's go. He's gone now. Last time my son, I said no, he said he ain't playing nothing, just one or two tunes, he…
